description: Experience the rich, aromatic flavors of our Mulligatawny Spiced Lentil Soup, a true Indian classic. This hearty and wholesome soup combines tender lentils with a vibrant medley of spices, vegetables, and a hint of coconut milk for a creamy finish. Perfect for a comforting meal, it offers a delightful balance of warmth and zest that will tantalize your taste buds.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear; drain well. Chop the onion, mince garlic, grate ginger, and prepare any other vegetables like diced apple or carrot if using.

instructions.title: Temper Spices
instructions.text: Heat ghee or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds; let them splutter for about 30 seconds. Add fresh curry leaves and green chili (if using) and saute for another 30 seconds until fragrant.

instructions.title: Sauté Vegetables and Aromatics
instructions.text: Add the chopped onion to the pot and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for another 1-2 minutes until aromatic. If using, add the diced apple or carrot at this stage and cook for 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Ground Spices and Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Reduce heat to low. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and garam masala. Stir constantly for about 1 minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for an additional minute.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Finish and Season
instructions.text: Stir in the coconut milk and cook for another 2-3 minutes, just until heated through; do not boil after adding coconut milk. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove from heat, stir in the fresh lemon juice, and garnish generously with chopped fresh cilantro before serving.

tips: For a smoother soup, you can use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup after the lentils are cooked, leaving some texture.
Adjust the spice level by increasing or decreasing the green chili. For extra heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper with the other ground spices.
If you prefer a richer flavor, toast the lentils lightly in a dry pan for a few minutes before rinsing and adding them to the soup.
